name: Bagru hand block printing
summary: Bagru hand block printing is a registered Geographical Indication (2011) of Bagru and three neighbouring villages in Jaipur district, Rajasthan, practised by the hereditary Chhipa printer community using carved wooden blocks. Its classic Syahi-Begar style prints an iron 'syahi' (black) and alum 'begar' (red) mordant on harda-treated, off-white cotton and develops both colours in one alizarin/madder dyebath; its Dabu style uses a black-clay resist paste followed by indigo and yellow dyeing.
